applicabilityBasis.summary: USDO is a yield-distributing rebasing product whose current issuer FAQ provides primary redemption into USDC and expressly says direct USD fiat redemption is unavailable. GENIUS section 2(22)(A)(ii)(I) excludes redemption into a digital asset denominated in fixed monetary value from the qualifying redemption obligation. The user agreement permits fiat where supported, so this scope assessment depends on the currently disclosed USDC-only redemption path and should be revisited if fiat redemption starts. Yield payment by itself is not a statutory scope exclusion.

references.label: GENIUS Act Public Law 119-27, payment stablecoin definition

genius.notes: USDO is a rebasing $1 token issued by OpenEden Digital Limited (the existing OpenEden Digital (OED) issuerEntity alias), acting for Segregated Account USDO in Bermuda. Current FAQ states that redemption is into USDC and that direct fiat USD redemption is only planned. The agreement includes fiat where supported, but also describes the holder contractual claim as USDC or other supported digital assets. This supports the non-payment-token scope assessment on currently available redemption rights, with medium confidence because the legal terms are broader than the live FAQ. The GENIUS Act interest prohibition in section 4(a)(11) is a separate issuer-conduct rule and does not automatically exclude yield-bearing tokens. U.S. persons are restricted by the agreement and minting eligibility page; that restriction alone does not determine statutory scope. Public reserve disclosure is present; a Chainlink proof-of-reserve feed is not a monthly independent accountant attestation. A 2026-10-07 OpenEden/USDO search restricted to OCC, SEC, CFTC, Treasury, DFS and FDIC domains did not locate a named public action; this does not establish the absence of nonpublic investigations.
